Headline: Ernie Johnson, the widely loved host of Inside the NBA, has announced he will step away at the end of the current season after 37 years in the role
Content: Ernie Johnson and Taylor Swift pose for a photo during last season’s NBA finals.Photograph: Jesse D Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenErnie Johnson and Taylor Swift pose for a photo during last season’s NBA finals.Photograph: Jesse D Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty ImagesUS sports mediaErnie Johnson, beloved host of Inside the NBA, to step away from show at end of season70-year-old wants to spend more time with familyJohnson leaving after 37 years in roleGuardian sportWed 28 Oct 2026 15.25 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 16.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleErnie Johnson,the widely loved host of Inside the NBA, has announced he will step away at the end of the current season after 37 years in the role.Johnson made the announcementon social media on Wednesday.“This is by no means the end,” Johnson said. “It’s just a turning of the page, and I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with Inside theNBA. And lastly, I just want to say thanks to you. Thanks for your loyalty, for your love, for your support, and on this day, for your understanding.”Inside the NBA: the sports gabfest that became late-night TV’s best showRead moreThe 70-year-old said he had undergone bypass surgery 14 months ago and wants to spend time with his wife and grandchildren. He has dealt with a series of health issues during his career. In 2003, he was diagnosed with non-Hodgkins lymphoma and he missed presenting duties during the 2018 MLB playoffs due to blood clots in his legs.Johnson joined Inside the NBA in 1990 and works alongside arguably the most popular panel of analysts in US sports: former NBA stars Kenny Smith, Charles Barkley and Shaquille O’Neal. Barkley has said he will retire from the show at the end of this season.During its run, Inside the NBA has won 19 Sports Emmys. In 2025 itmoved from its longtime homeon on Turner networks to ABC and ESPN.“Ernie Johnson is one of sports media’s most respected and beloved figures,”ESPNchairman Jimmy Pitaro said in a statement. “For more than three decades, he has been the heart of Inside the NBA, helping create one of the most iconic and entertaining studio shows in sports. We are grateful for Ernie’s extraordinary contributions and look forward to celebrating him throughout the season.”Explore more on these topicsUS sports mediaNBAABCESPNBasketballUS television industryUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progress | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Liverpool won penalty shootout in which there were five failed kicks 6-5 after a 1-1 draw with Chelsea in the Carabao Cup at Anfield
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Liverpool won penalty shootout in which there were five failed kicks 6-5 after a 1-1 draw with Chelsea in the Carabao Cup at Anfield
Content: Wesley Fofana lifts his penalty over the bar and Liverpool go through.Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenWesley Fofana lifts his penalty over the bar and Liverpool go through.Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty ImagesCarabao CupLiverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progressAndy Hunterat AnfieldWed 28 Oct 2026 18.30 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 20.21 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea must have been resigned to their fate as soon as the shootout arrived at Anfield. Four times they had faced Liverpool on penalties previously and four times they had lost. Number five was confirmed when Wesley Fofana’s wild effort sailed high into the Kop and sent Andoni Iraola’s side into aCarabao Cupquarter-final against his old club Bournemouth.Fofana was not the only culprit as Chelsea’s catalogue of penalty misery againstLiverpoolgained a new chapter alongside the 2007 Champions League semi-final, the 2019 Uefa Super Cup final and the FA and League Cup finals of 2022.Liverpool beat Chelsea 6-5 on penalties: Carabao Cup reaction and quarter-final draw – liveRead moreEmmanuel Emegha had the chance to win it for Xabi Alonso’s side in sudden death but was denied superbly by Giorgi Mamardashvili. Liverpool fluffed their lines with victory in sight too, Kostas Tsimikas blazing over and ruining the chance to reprise his match-winning role at Wembley four years ago. Ryan Gravenberch and Valentin Barco also failed to convert.It fell to Joe Gomez of all people to edge Liverpool ahead with the first shootout penalty of his Anfield career. The long-serving defender, who has never scored for Liverpool, found the top corner of Mike Penders’s goal in convincing style. Fofana could not repeat the trick and finally, after Morgan Rogers and Cody Gakpo had both scored penalties in normal time, the two adversaries were separated. It was another painful result for Alonso, fresh from the home defeat against Tottenham on Saturday, although theChelseadisplay was an improvement.The Chelsea manager said: “For sure it is not the outcome we wanted or expected but once you go to penalties there has to be a sad side. We played with courage, the game was close with not many chances for both sides. It is a small setback because it is probably the least important competition for us. As soon as we leave Anfield our focus will be on a very important game [against Manchester United] on Saturday.”If, as Alonso claimed, the Carabao Cup is not a priority for Chelsea this season then his decision to again overlook the merits of Estêvão, who was left kicking his heels on the bench all evening, was mystifying. With João Pedro injured and Cole Palmer suspended Chelsea started with Danny Welbeck in attack and the former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson operating in an advanced midfield role. Liverpool contained them relatively comfortably.View image in fullscreenAndoni Iraola embraces his goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesThe Premier League rivals served up a fast-paced, committed cup tie that was lacking goalmouth incident before they exchanged penalties in the space of four minutes. Chelsea were awarded the first when Moisés Caicedo was released inside the Liverpool area by a cleverly disguised pass from Malo Gusto and clipped from behind by Gravenberch. The boos for Henderson intensified as he carried the ball to the spot with a wry smile on his face and handed it to Rogers, who sent Mamardashvili the wrong way with an emphatic penalty kick.Liverpool soon had a spot-kick of their own when Caicedo and Fofana challenged Virgil van Dijk at a Tsimikas corner and the ball struck the Chelsea defender’s raised hand. Gakpo converted confidently into the bottom corner. The referee, Darren England, called both penalties instantly and correctly, showing officials do not always have to rely on video assistance. The game benefited as a spectacle from the absence of a video assistant referee, although Iraola might well have disagreed had Rogers scored after appearing to control Pedro Neto’s chip with his arm. Mamardashvili’s save meant that controversy was avoided.Penders, keen to atone for his costly error against Spurs, took centre stage for Chelsea when saving a flying header from Ronald Araújo at close range. The Liverpool defender had been supplied by a fine cross from Gomez and, with two defenders pushed forwards, Rogers almost punished them on the counterattack. Gomez, however, worked tirelessly to chase back and block the forward’s eventual shot. Penders also saved impressively from Bradley Barcola when the France international cut inside from the right and his low shot was deflected towards the bottom corner.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideCarabao Cup quarter-final drawShowFleetwood v Everton or NewcastleManchester City v Bradford CityCrystal Palace v SunderlandLiverpool v BournemouthTies will take place during the week commencing 14 DecemberWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Rogers was involved in several promising openings for Chelsea as Alonso’s team – improved more than Liverpool by their substitutes – finished strongly. Marco Palestra had the best of them when released by the England forward’s perfectly weighted pass but Mamardashvili produced an excellent save low to his right. Wirtz also had a late chance to seal victory but his attempt from Gakpo’s knock-down struck Levi Colwill and was eventually cleared. And so to penalties, and a familiar feeling for the side from Stamford Bridge.Iraola said: “I’m pleased for the players because they put in a big effort tonight. I can feel [togetherness within the squad] and I’m happy to feel it because it is very important. The players are feeling support from the crowd and now we have another big one on Sunday [against Arsenal] so let’s try to finish this four in a row in the best way.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupLiverpoolChelseamatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Dream say WNBA finals concerns went unheeded as teams prepare for 12.30pm Thursday start  | WNBA | The Guardian
description: The Atlanta Dream say their concerns about finding a suitable home venue for the WNBA finals went unheeded as they prepare to play the Golden State Valkyries
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The Atlanta Dream say their concerns about finding a suitable home venue for the WNBA finals went unheeded as they prepare to play the Golden State Valkyries
Content: The 2026 WNBA finals have seen a series of hard-fought games.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe 2026 WNBA finals have seen a series of hard-fought games.Photograph: Ezra Shaw/Getty ImagesWNBADream say WNBA finals concerns went unheeded as teams prepare for 12.30pm Thursday startCrucial Game 6 will take place on Thursday afternoonGame moved to larger State Farm Arena in AtlantaHawks’ NBA game on same day could not be movedGuardian sportWed 28 Oct 2026 08.24 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 08.26 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Atlanta Dream say their concerns aboutfinding a suitable home venuefor the WNBA finals went unheeded as they prepare to play the Golden State Valkyries in a crucial Game 6 on Thursday.The Dream’s normal home, Gateway Center Arena, has a capacity of about 3,500 people. To accommodate the increased interest in the team during the finals, the Dream have played their two home games so far at theAtlantaHawks’ State Farm Arena, which can seat more than 17,000 fans.The WNBA finals are a basketball wonderland – unless you’re part of the Maga machineRead moreHowever, the Hawks play the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night, meaning the Dream and Valkyries will play Game 6 at 12.30pm EDT on the same day. That means Valkyries fans in their home state of California will watch the game at 9.30am local time.Golden State lead the best-of-seven series 3-2.In an open letter to their fans on Tuesday, the Dream said they had raised concerns about a possible scheduling clash months ago, but the calls went unheeded.“This incredible run by our players has … made something else abundantly clear: theAtlanta Dreamhas earned the right to be taken seriously,” the Dream wrote in the letter. “Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena. As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved.”The letter did not elaborate on the exact concerns the team raised, or who they raised them with at theWNBA.According to ESPN, WNBA teams were told the dates for this season’s playoffs in December 2025.The WNBA, NBA, Dream, Golden State and the finals’ broadcasting partners had discussions over the weekend about the best solution to the venue problem. In Tuesday’s letter, the Dream said playing Game 6 during the afternoon was the best option available.“As much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage,” the letter said. “That meant State Farm Arena.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Valkyries’ Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton have urged fans to call in sick so they can see their team potentially clinch the title in only their second season in the WNBA. Meanwhile, the Dream’s Allisha Gray said her main focus was the game itself, not the start time.“It’s the finals,” Gray said. “We just got to do what we’ve got to do. We are locked in on winning Game 6 whether it’s 8am, 10pm, midnight. We got a championship to win.”Explore more on these topicsWNBAAtlanta DreamGolden State ValkyriesBasketballUS sportsAtlantaWest CoastnewsShareReuse this content

title: Jay-Z is the perfect Super Bowl shill for a league of billionaires | NFL | The Guardian
description: The rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the league
Author: Lee Escobedo
Headline: The rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the league
Content: NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and Jay-Z greet each other at the announcement of NFL and Roc Nation’s agreement in 2019.Photograph: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc NationView image in fullscreenNFL commissioner Roger Goodell and Jay-Z greet each other at the announcement of NFL and Roc Nation’s agreement in 2019.Photograph: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Roc NationNFLJay-Z is the perfect Super Bowl shill for a league of billionairesLee EscobedoThe rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the leagueWed 28 Oct 2026 05.15 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 06.51 EDTShareOn Monday the NFLnamed Jay-Zas the headliner for this season’s Super Bowl half-time show. His company, Roc Nation, produces the show under a 2019 dealreportedlyworth $5m a year, and the agreement was extended for another five years in 2024. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said his one request when the partnership began was that Jay-Z “take the stage himself one day“.Goodell’s wish makes total sense:Jay-Zis the perfect choice for the half-time show, and that’s not a compliment. The NFL wants a shill who can still pass for a rebel, and nobody in American music plays that part better than Jay-Z.Colin Kaepernick knelt 10 years ago. America responded with a clear warning to Black people | Howard BryantRead moreJay-Z’s origin story has become an American legend. Years before he sold records, Shawn Carter grew up in Brooklyn’s Marcy Houses andsold crackas a teenager. When labels passed on him, he hawked CDs from the trunk of his car on college campuses. Then he put out Reasonable Doubt in 1996 on his own label, Roc-A-Fella. “Nobody would sign me,” he said later. The money followed. In 2013, he performed Picasso Baby, a track about the paintings he wanted to own, for six hours straight at aChelsea gallery, and Marina Abramović joined him. By the time of The Story of OJ in 2017, he washanding out financial advice. Forbes puts his fortune at about$2.8bn. He raps for the rich now, a Black oligarch who seems about as cut off from the rest of the country as the rest of the billionaire class.His bootstraps story mirrors the platitudes Americans have been told for decades – work hard and you’ll get what you deserve. On paper, he’s the perfect avatar for America’s polluted ideas of capitalism. But the country Jay-Z is rapping to is in terrible shape. How many of us can relate to his lyrics in 2026? Gas and grocery prices have rocketed. SNAP enrollmentfell more than 13%in a year as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act tightened the rules. Only 63% of adults say they couldcover a surprise $400 expense.You can see why the NFL would use Jay-Z as someone who can give the appearance that the league, with its huge conservative fanbase, is actually progressive. Hewore Colin Kaepernick’s jerseyon Saturday Night Live in 2017 after the quarterback had sparked a protest movement against police brutality by kneeling for the national anthem. Jay-Z then dedicated The Story of OJ to Kaepernick onstage. A year later, on Apeshit, he bragged about turning down the Super Bowl and told the NFL it needed him more than he needed it.Things would soon change.In June 2019, Forbes named himhip-hop’s first billionaire. A few months later, Roc Nation signed its deal with the NFL. But at the news conference announcing his NFL partnership, Jay-Z no longer appeared as receptive to Kaepernick’s approach to protest. “We’vemoved past kneeling,” he said. That same year, Kaepernicksettled his collusion grievanceagainst the league after he said his protests had effectively ended his playing career.The 2019 deal also put Roc Nation to work onInspire Change, the league’s social justice initiative. It’s safe to say that Kaepernick was unimpressed. “I just want you to know, one, you’re serving the culture up to a bunch of racists and, two, they don’t care about you,” Kaepernicklater recalled saying to Jay-Z. “You’re the music guy to them. They quite literally need a Black face – and have said as much.”Seven years later, Jay-Z is still battling Kaepernick, the man who says he was blackballed by the NFL. This summer, Jay-Z linked up with Target, whichhad been boycottedby many Black customers after it rolled back its diversity and inclusion policies. Kaepernick, on the other hand, said he would not allow his memoir to be sold at any of the chain’s stores. At a concert in July, Jay-Z rapped that Kaepernick had allowed himself to be silenced by signing his grievance with the NFL (sources close to Kaepernickhave denied this). “Buddy took a check, I ain’t even mad at him, but along with that check you have to sign a non-disparagement. I’m the one [the NFL] can’t control,” Jay-Z rapped to the crowd at Yankee Stadium.Maybe that’s true, but it doesn’t appear that Jay-Z is doing much to control – or change – the league either. In 2021,USA Today’s Mike Freeman wrote: “There isn’t a single, tangible thing you can point to that shows Jay-Z helping with the league’s social justice efforts.” That’s a little unfair; through Inspire Changethe NFL has funnelled millionsinto charities across America. At the same time, the NFL is mostly run by the same old, rich conservatives it always has been. There is still no Black majority owner of a team, and Forbes now puts the combined value of theleague’s 32 teamsat more than $300bn. In 2025, Donald Trump, who once called NFL players who protested during the national anthem“sons of bitches”, becamethe first sitting president to attend a Super Bowl, and that same week the leaguepulled “End Racism”from the endzones in New Orleans. That slogan had been on NFL fields since 2020 as part of Inspire Change.Conservatives have noticed. Acolumnpublished onSport & Statehailed Jay-Z as a “legend” and told readers there likely wouldn’t be any anti-ICE activists onstage at this season’s halftime show, adding that “after last year’s Bad Bunny debacle, Jay-Z offers a compromise.”That’s about right. Jay-Z won’t have anybody to push against at theSuper Bowl. The NFL is Roc Nation’s client, and the team owners are its partners. As we saw with the Target debacle, whatever Jay-Z says up there, he’s unlikely to go against the people who pay him.Explore more on these topicsNFLSuper BowlJay-ZUS sportsColin KaepernickcommentShareReuse this content

title: New study estimates 75% of deceased ex-NFL players had brain disease CTE | US news | The Guardian
description: Research looked at prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 2,362 players who died in 2008-2023
Author: Marina Dunbar
Headline: Research looked at prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 2,362 players who died in 2008-2023
Content: Dr Ann McKee, director of Boston University’s CTE Center, analyzes brain tissue on 31 May 2017.Photograph: Stan Grossfeld/The Boston Globe via Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenDr Ann McKee, director of Boston University’s CTE Center, analyzes brain tissue on 31 May 2017.Photograph: Stan Grossfeld/The Boston Globe via Getty ImagesUS newsNew study estimates 75% of deceased ex-NFL players had brain disease CTEResearch looked at prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy in 2,362 players who died in 2008-2023Marina DunbarWed 28 Oct 2026 14.04 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 15.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA new study published on Wednesday estimates that about 75% of formerNFLplayers who died over a 15-year period had evidence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE).The research, published inJama Network Openand conducted by a Boston-based team, examined the estimated prevalence of the degenerative brain disease among NFL players who died from 2008 through 2023. Researchers found that the estimated rate of CTE among these players was substantially higher than the rates observed in brain samples collected from the general population.The analysis included records from 2,362 deceased former NFL players who spent an average of five years in the league. Of the nearly 400 players whose brains were donated for examination, 93.5% showed evidence of CTE.Researchers said the findings represented the first attempt to estimate how widespread CTE was among all former NFL players who died during the 2008-2023 period, rather than limiting the analysis to individuals whose brains were donated for research.CTE in football players is a health crisis. It’s time for us to stop watchingRead morePhysical changes associated with the condition include brain atrophy, which involves the loss of brain tissue, and accumulations of tau protein, a characteristic also associated with Alzheimer’s disease.The difference compared with the broader population was substantial. According to the study’s authors, less than 1% of brain samples from community-based brain banks contain evidence of CTE.However, the presence of CTE-related changes in the brain does not necessarily mean a person will develop dementia or experience declining cognitive abilities. Some individuals with the condition may never develop noticeable symptoms.Researchers estimated that approximately 27% of the former NFL players included in the analysis had dementia.CTE can also damage areas of the brain responsible for emotional control and behavior. Potential symptoms include depression, memory problems, severe mood changes and other behavioral difficulties.“We recognize these findings may cause concern for the community of living players and their families,” Yorghos Tripodis, the study’s senior author, said in a statement released byMass General Brigham. “We want them to know that we and others are standing by to provide support, and that we have hope for those living with CTE.“Discoveries from the brain bank have already brought us significantly closer to a diagnosis during life, at which point our most important goal will be to develop effective treatments for CTE,” Tripodis added.The findings followanother studyreleased in August, which determined that at least one in four of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE.Following the publication of the earlier study, the NFL addressed its efforts to improve player safety in a statement: “The NFL continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing ⁠strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.”A number of high-profile NFL players who took their own lives – including Junior Seau, Dave Duerson and Aaron Hernandez – were found to have had CTE when their brains were analyzed after their deaths.Explore more on these topicsUS newsNFLUS sportsHealthMedical researchnewsShareReuse this content

title: Max Dowman’s Fleetwood fracas leaves him, Arsenal and Arteta red-faced | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Teenager was maybe harshly sent off in the Carabao Cup tie but his reaction was a mistake he will learn from, while his manager might also have regrets
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Teenager was maybe harshly sent off in the Carabao Cup tie but his reaction was a mistake he will learn from, while his manager might also have regrets
Content: Mikel Arteta lets Max Dowman know exactly what he thinks after the 16-year-old was sent off late in the Carabao Cup tie at Fleetwood.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta lets Max Dowman know exactly what he thinks after the 16-year-old was sent off late in the Carabao Cup tie at Fleetwood.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesArsenalMax Dowman’s Fleetwood fracas leaves him, Arsenal and Arteta red-facedTeenager was maybe harshly sent off in the Carabao Cup tie but his reaction was a mistake he will learn from, while his manager might also have regretsEd AaronsWed 28 Oct 2026 09.16 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 12.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Arteta’s reaction said it all. As Max Dowman trudged towards the touchline after becoming the youngest player sent off in a League Cup match at 16 years and 300 days, the Arsenal manager could not help himself.Arms folded across his chest like an angry father who has caught his teenage son sneaking in after midnight, Arteta leaned over and aimed a few choice words in Dowman’s direction before the forward headed sheepishly down the tunnel. What he said remains unknown, although that hasn’t stopped the amateur lip-readers speculating on social media. “Get in the changing room. Now,” appears the most likely guess.‘What you live for’: Fleetwood revel in seismic Arsenal shock after Dowman sees redRead moreThere is no doubt Arteta had made up his mind about the incident that ended with Dowman seeing red for reacting to an overaggressive sliding tackle from Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal. Although Arsenal intend to appeal and Arteta told Sky afterthe shock penalty shootout defeatby the League Two side 84 places below them in the pyramid that he wanted to watch it again before “assessing the situation”, the Spaniard made no excuses for Dowman in his post-match press conference.“It was something that we discussed before the game,” he said when asked about their touchline exchange. “We knew when we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to expect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate.”Whether Dowman’s reaction warranted a straight red card remains open to debate given there was minimal force when he lifted his right knee towards Neal. The referee, Michael Salisbury, could easily have decided to give both players a yellow and defused the situation, especially givenCole Palmer was booked for barging into Tottenham’s Matheus Fernandesoff the ball on Saturday in what seemed a far more aggressive act. But, as Wayne Rooney and David Beckham infamously found to their cost while playing for England at the World Cup, acts of petulance are not usually tolerated by officials. Dowman was deemed to have overstepped the line.It is a pressure Arteta has warned the record-breaking teenager would have to deal with as Dowman’s reputation has grown. Only last month Dowman was sent off playing for England Under-19s against the USA after a poorly timed tackle that most present at the behind-closed-doors match deemed a harsh decision. He was said to have been on the receiving end of a host of strong challenges in that match. Last year, Arteta urged Dowman to follow the example of Bukayo Saka after revealing Dowman was fouled nine times in a the first half of an England Under‑19s game against Spain.View image in fullscreenMax Dowman is the centre of attention for Fleetwood’s players after the teenager’s reaction to a tackle from Harrison Neal.Photograph: Ryan Browne/Shutterstock“It’s going to happen, he’s going to have to learn when to release the ball and when to attract his starting position,” Arteta said. “Very similar to Bukayo in the beginning as well. Those players are going to attract players, contact, attention and they have to be very smart about when you want that contact and when you don’t want it, and what you have to do to avoid it.”Asked how Dowman tends to react, he said: “He just gets up … very rare! Sometimes I get surprised emotionally how cool he can be. I think it’s about repetition. He’s so used to it that now he knows to let the referee deal with it and my teammates probably to defend me, and I will carry on playing.”When the dust settles after a seismic defeat that ranks alongside Arsenal’s League Cup upsets against Swindon, Birmingham and Bradford, Arteta may come to regret such a public admonishment of a 16-year-old. His actions were criticised by Paul Merson, who questioned whether Areta would “do it differently” given another chance. But part of Arteta’s frustration will be that Dowman took the bait. He also knows opponents will now target Dowman even more to see whether they can provoke a reaction.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIf Arsenal’s appeal fails, Dowman’s immediate punishment will be a three-match domestic suspension, causing him to miss Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and games against Hull and Newcastle. The timing is far from helpful:Saka’s thigh injury, expected to keep him out for several weeks, had opened up the possibility of more game time in the Premier League and Noni Madueke did not travel to Fleetwood owing to an ankle issue.Dowman burst on to the scene last year by becoming the first 15-year-old to play in the Champions League, then broke the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer record against Everton in March, and this is the first major setback in his fledgling career.He has been training with the first team since he was 14 and Arsenal have been extremely careful not to overexpose one of the most talked about players to emerge from their Hale End academy. Arteta resisted the temptation to give him many more minutes in the Premier League after Dowmanscored twice against Ipswich in the previous roundof the Carabao Cup last month. The challenge will be how Dowman responds to the extra scrutiny – on and off the pitch – that is bound to come his way.Explore more on these topicsArsenalCarabao CupMikel ArtetafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Rays battle from brink in 12th inning to stun Brewers and stave off World Series sweep | World Series | The Guardian
description: Tampa Bay kept their flickering championship hopes alive with a dramatic 12th-inning rally against Milwaukee in Game 4 of the World Series
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Tampa Bay kept their flickering championship hopes alive with a dramatic 12th-inning rally against Milwaukee in Game 4 of the World Series
Content: Tampa Bay players mob Ben Williamson after his walk-off RBI single in the 12th inning secured a Game 4 victory over Milwaukee and kept their World Series hopes alive on Tuesday night.Photograph: Al Bello/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTampa Bay players mob Ben Williamson after his walk-off RBI single in the 12th inning secured a Game 4 victory over Milwaukee and kept their World Series hopes alive on Tuesday night.Photograph: Al Bello/Getty ImagesWorld SeriesRays battle from brink in 12th inning to stun Brewers and stave off World Series sweepTampa Bay force Game 5 with extra-innings rallyMilwaukee denied first World Series championshipBrewers still hold 3-1 lead in best-of-seven seriesAgenciesWed 28 Oct 2026 00.54 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 07.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson hits RBIs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over theMilwaukee Brewerson Tuesday night that forced Game 5.Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for his fourth hit of the game to make it 3-2 to the Brewers as Milwaukee neared a sweep and their firstWorld Seriestitle.But the Rays, also seeking their first championship, rallied in the bottom half after a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz on Junior Caminero’s leadoff grounder against reliever Antonio Senzatela.Liam Hicks singled off Shane Drohan, who relieved in his first appearance since 15 October, and DeLuca’s single to center drove in pinch-runner Cedric Mullins to tie the score at 3-3.Quick GuideWorld Series 2026ShowScheduleBest-of-seven series. All times US Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).Fri 23 OctGame 1:Milwaukee 3, Tampa Bay 2Sat 24 OctGame 2:Milwaukee 5, Tampa Bay 4Mon 26 OctGame 3:Milwaukee 10, Tampa Bay 1Tue 27 OctGame 4:Tampa Bay 4, Milwaukee 3 (12 innings)Wed 28 OctGame 5: Milwaukee at Tampa Bay, 8pm (Fox)Fri 30 OctGame 6: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)Sat 31 OctGame 7: Tampa Bay at Milwaukee, 8pm* (Fox)*-if necessaryHow to watchIn the US, all World Series games will air on Fox and Fox Deportes, with streaming available through Fox One. In the UK, the series will be carried by TNT Sports. In Australia, fans can watch on ESPN, with streaming available through Disney+ and Kayo Sports.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Chandler Simpson’s single loaded the bases and Milwaukee employed a five-man infield.Williamson, who had been 1 for 15 in the postseason, hit a chopper over first baseman Jake Bauers and into right field to clinch the 4-3 win for the Rays.“We’ve got a lot of fight in us. We’re never going to shy away,” Simpson said. “We were going to keep fighting until the end – the last inning, the last out, the last play, the last pitch. We were going to keep fighting. That’s what we did tonight.”Game 5 in the best-of-seven matchup is Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, with NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski scheduled to start for the Brewers. Rays manager Kevin Cash said he hadn’t decided on a starter yet.Tampa Bay are just the fifth of 26 teams to have fallen behind 3-0 in the World Series and then come back to win Game 4. The previous four lost Game 5.Of 43 teams to trail 3-0 in any best-of-seven postseason matchup, the only one who rebounded to win was the Boston Red Sox against the New York Yankees in the 2004 American League Championship Series.“It just shows the resiliency of this group,” Williamson said. “We continue to fight, and that’s been the motto this series and this full season, is just fight.”Caminero was replaced by Mullins at third base and hobbled off the field with an ailing left foot. But the slugger said he’ll definitely play Wednesday night.“He’ll play tomorrow on one leg. I’ll make sure of it,” Cash said.View image in fullscreenBrewers infielder David Hamilton attempts to tag Rays runner Junior Caminero during the fourth inning of Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night.Photograph: Mike Stobe/Getty ImagesTampa Bay ended an eight-game winning streak by the Brewers, who were bidding to become only the second team to sweep a League Championship Series and the World Series.“If you want to win a championship, you’ve got to survive some hard things,” Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich said. “Like I said earlier, it’s supposed to be hard. It’s supposed to test you. We understand that.”David Hamilton also homered for the Brewers. Jackson Chourio had a single and double, improving to 10 for 20 in the Series.Pratt, a 22-year-old rookie whose go-ahead hit sparked the Brewers to a 5-4 win in Game 2, drove a slider into the left-field seats against Seymour. Pratt had tied the score at 1 with an RBI double in the second.Milwaukee players bounded out of the dugout to greet Pratt, who debuted in June and became the first rookie to hit an extra-inning homer in the World Series.Seymour had allowed Frelick’s tying homer in Game 2.View image in fullscreenRays outfielder Jonny DeLuca scores a run in the second inning against the Brewers during Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night at Tropicana Field.Photograph: Carmen Mandato/Getty ImagesMilwaukee fans in the crowd of 40,514, many waving yellow towels and some wearing cheeseheads, brought a Badger State feel to Tropicana Field.Tampa Bay returned to their white home jerseys, a day after playing in Devil Rays throwbacks.Simpson hit an RBI double off starter Dustin May in the second, but Milwaukee tied the score in the fourth against Griffin Jax when Frelick hit a two-out single and came around on Pratt’s double.Caminero singled leading off the bottom half to chase May and advanced on a groundout. DeLuca hit a hard grounder to Hamilton and Caminero twisted toward the grass to avoid the third baseman’s tag, then came home when Hamilton bounced his throw past Bauers for an error.Hamilton, Milwaukee’s No 9 hitter, drove an 0-2 fastball at the letters from Jax into the right-field seats for his second home run of the postseason – half his regular-season total and just his second since 6 June.Explore more on these topicsWorld SeriesTampa Bay RaysMilwaukee BrewersBaseballUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Fernandes tells Carrick he is committed to turning season around in clear-the-air talks | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is expected to return to the starting lineup against Chelsea on Saturday after talks with Michael Carrick
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is expected to return to the starting lineup against Chelsea on Saturday after talks with Michael Carrick
Content: Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held talks at Carrington on Tuesday after their falling-out.Photograph: David Davies/PAView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held talks at Carrington on Tuesday after their falling-out.Photograph: David Davies/PAManchester UnitedFernandes tells Carrick he is committed to turning season around in clear-the-air talksManchester United captain expected to return to lineupSquad have positive meeting with under-pressure coachJamie JacksonWed 28 Oct 2026 08.47 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 15.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes held clear-the-air talks on Tuesday after theManchester Unitedcaptain criticised the head coach’s tactics last week, with the player now expected to start at Chelsea on Saturday.Carrick and Fernandes met before training on Tuesday morning at United’s Carrington training base. The 32-year-old captain, it is understood, offered assurances that he is fully committed and intent on trying to turn the team’s season around. There was also a squad meeting with Carrick at which the rest of the players made the same vow.An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeurRead moreDismal results have left Carrick’s job in the balance. Later on Tuesday it emerged thatthe 45-year-old will remain in charge for the trip to Chelseaafter Jason Wilcox, the director of football, decided he should be given more time.But to remain as the head coach for the long term, Carrick has to start winning games. So having dropped Fernandes, who is considered United’s best player, for the3-0 home defeat by Bournemouthon Sunday because of the criticism, the captain now being available for Chelsea is a considerable boost.After the4-1 defeat at Comolast Wednesday, Fernandes questioned the team’s strategy. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man‑to‑man,” he said. As Carrick decides tactics, this was seen as a direct attack on the head coach.On Wednesday morning Kobbie Mainoo was back in training after missing the past four games because of injury.Carrick’s side have won twice in 12 games and were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Brighton. United are 16th in the Premier League, a point above the relegation zone.United host Roma in the Champions League three days after playing Chelsea, then Aston Villa in the league the following Sunday before a two-week international window, which would offer a longer period for the board to assess the situation.Carrick’s reprieve may be a move to allow time for Wilcox to secure a replacement should the decision be taken to sack the head coach. The director of football’s prime candidate is the former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, while Christopher Vivell, the head of recruitment, favours the former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann.United believe Benjamin Sesko will be out until January due to a shin injury. The 23-year-old has been out since the3-2 Carabao Cup defeat by Brightonon 16 September, with the problem relating to a kick he received to the shin in the closing months of last season.Sesko is Carrick’s only recognised senior centre-forward. The head coach has often fielded Bryan Mbeumo and Fernandes as false 9s in his absence.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Arsenal’s Slegers hails ‘role model’ Russo after historic hat-trick sinks Benfica | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Alessia Russo’s hat-trick made her the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League, as Arsenal cruised to a 3-0 win against Benfica
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: Alessia Russo’s hat-trick made her the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League, as Arsenal cruised to a 3-0 win against Benfica
Content: Alessia Russo (No 23) celebrates with her teammates after making it 2-0 against Benfica.Photograph: David Cliff/EPAView image in fullscreenAlessia Russo (No 23) celebrates with her teammates after making it 2-0 against Benfica.Photograph: David Cliff/EPAWomen's Champions LeagueArsenal’s Slegers hails ‘role model’ Russo after historic hat-trick sinks BenficaSophie Downeyat Mangata Developments StadiumWed 28 Oct 2026 18.21 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 20.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlessia Russo wrote herself into the history books once more as she became the highest English goalscorer in the Women’s Champions League. Her hat-trick gave Arsenal a vital 3-0 win against Benfica to send the Gunners up to second in the league phase table.“I’m so happy. I think we’ve found a nice dynamic as well with the last two games,” Russo’s manager, Renée Slegers, said. “She’s one of the leaders and she does it her way. She cares for everyone around her and connects well with her teammates. She leads the way as a role model, doing the right things consistently.”It was a statement performance from the 27-year-old who has shaken off the early-season cobwebs. Her three goals at Meadow Park on Wednesday took her tally up to 10 in her past seven appearances for club and country, hitting a rich vein of form just when Arsenal have needed her most.Arsenal 3-0 Benfica: Women’s Champions League – as it happenedRead moreIt is safe to say Arsenal’s season has yet to fully burst into life. Struggles in front of goal and unforced errors have defined the opening two months but the grittynorth London derby winon Saturday did feel like it could be a springboard for momentum.There was no less pressure coming into this Champions League match against Benfica, another must-win game with Arsenal’s European form mirroring their domestic struggles. A last-ditchwin against HB Køgeand a heartbreaking draw against Paris FC (in which they surrendered a two‑goal lead) left them fifth in the league phase table before kick-off, with Barcelona and OL Lyonnes looming.Slegers made three changes to freshen things up. Ona Batlle returned to her more natural right‑back role while the summer signings Élisa De Almeida and Géraldine Reuteler made their full debuts.Ivan Baptista’s Benfica arrived in confident form on the back of consecutive wins domestically. Slegers was keen to highlight their strong identity pre-match, having had first‑hand experience of their resilience in last year’s league phase. So it proved once more in a first half in which Arsenal dominated, but struggled to break through against a well-structured opposition.View image in fullscreenThe Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, has eased pressure on herself with back-to-back wins over Spurs and Benfica.Photograph: David Cliff/EPAIt was the visitors, in fact, who had the best opportunity of the first half hour. Frøya Dorsin was left beating the turf in frustration after spurning a glorious opportunity to catch out a stranded Misa Rodríguez with a lob. It was a moment that jolted Arsenal into life as they upped the tempo and began to rain pressure on Benfica’s goal. First Olivia Smith set up Russo for a low shot that went narrowly wide before Smith herself forced Lena Pauels into a fine save.Arsenal found their breakthrough just before half-time when Russo produced a sublime finish after a well‑worked move down the left.It was like a switch had flipped for Arsenal after the break as they exuded confidence, zipping the ball around the turf with increasing ease. Smith looked more and more comfortable in her central role while Caitlin Foord came alive down the left, the latter denied a clear shot by a superb last-ditch challenge.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe conductor behind them all was Russo as she pressed and stretched the play to her tune. The captain on the night was at the heart of things once more as the hosts doubled their lead, rising high to glance home a corner. She completed her hat-trick shortly afterwards, converting from the spot after Foord was brought down by Catarina Amado.Quick GuideRoundup: Chelsea roll past Roma, Bayern and Real drawShowChelsea maintained their strong start to this year’s Women’s Champions League campaign as second-half goals from Ellie Carpenter [pictured, centre] and Kadeisha Buchanan secured a 2-0 win over Roma at Plough Lane.After a goalless first half, substitute Carpenter combined with Wieke Kaptein to open the scoring in the 51st minute. The Australian made a powerful run, found Kaptein and then met her cross from the right with a low shot which took a deflection off Roma defender Winonah Heatley before going in.Central defender Buchanan wrapped up the win in the 89th minute, heading home to ensure a second win in three European matches for Sonia Bompastor’s unbeaten team. Roma were left to rue chances missed by Maya Doms and Alayah Pilgrim as they extended their scoreless Champions League start to three games.'I’m pleased with the fact we scored really early in the second half. We could probably have killed the game a little bit earlier,' said the Chelsea head coach, Sonia Bompastor. 'It’s important for us in these games to be able to be clinical and ruthless as early as possible. But we find different ways to impose ourselves in the game and to score goals. So it’s good.'Bayern Munichfought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 againstReal Madridand preserve their unbeaten home record in the pre-knockout phase. Last season’s semi-finalists have now not lost any of their 17 home games in the group stage or league phase thanks to Momoko Tanikawa's second-half equaliser.Athenea del Castillo pounced from Linda Caicedo’s cross in the seventh minute, before Lineth Beerensteyn headed in from close range to double Madrid’s lead midway through the first half. Edna Imade nodded in to reduce the deficit on the half-hour and Tanikawa levelled soon after the restart, before Sophie Proost hit the post for Bayern in stoppage time.Eight-time championsLyonnescruised to an emphatic 6-0 home victory overInternazionale, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring twice before Lily Yohannes made it three on the hour mark. Vicki Bècho came off the bench shortly after and hit a hat-trick as the French giants went top of the table on goal difference.Swiss sideServetteclaimed a historic maiden Champions League win at the ninth attempt as they brushed aside OH Leuven 5-1 in Geneva. Paola Hernández and Gloria Marinelli both struck twice to leave the Belgian champions winless so far in this season’s league phase.Press AssociationPhotograph: Andrew Redington/Getty Images EuropeWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.It was a finish that marked the 200th goal of Slegers’s tenure and one that further eases the pressure on the head coach. With every minute that passed the hosts looked increasingly like themselves and could have added more to their tally.“It looks like there is something off our shoulders,” Slegers said. “We were playing like us tonight and I am so happy. The players enjoyed themselves – they connected, they expressed themselves and they played with intensity. We backed the last performance up. We need to do it again at the weekend.”There will no doubt be sterner tests to come in Europe, more immediately away to Barcelona in a fortnight’s time, but this was a victory that signified something more important than just climbing up the Champions League table.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueArsenal WomenBenfica womenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Rulli’s heroics earn Manchester City shootout success against Brighton | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: The goalkeeper saved spot-kicks from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk in Manchester City’s 4-3 shootout win after the Carabao Cup match finished 2-2
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The goalkeeper saved spot-kicks from Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk in Manchester City’s 4-3 shootout win after the Carabao Cup match finished 2-2
Content: Gerónimo Rulli is congratulated by teammates after Manchester City’s dramatic win.Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenGerónimo Rulli is congratulated by teammates after Manchester City’s dramatic win.Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty ImagesCarabao CupRulli’s heroics earn Manchester City shootout success against BrightonJamie Jacksonat the Etihad StadiumWed 28 Oct 2026 17.58 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 21.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter Jérémy Doku’s second-half substitute appearance transformedManchester Cityinto a high-octane proposition, the smart money was on the momentum continuing into a victorious penalty shootout.So it proved as Enzo Maresca’s men triumphed 4-3, Gerónimo Rulli the hero: his save from Lewis Dunk’s fifth spot-kick was decisive, the Argentinean also having repelled Yasin Ayari’s fourth effort.Nketiah takes Crystal Palace past Fulham and earns Sage breathing spaceRead moreWhile Jason Steele kept out Mateo Kovacic’s attempt, City progressed after Brighton twice took the lead – via Malick Yalcouyé and Georginio Rutter – before being pegged back by Kovacic and Vitor Reis.Maresca was left beaming: “Since I’m here we never practised penalties,” said the City manager. “It always happens that the one that scored in the 90 minutes [Kovacic] misses the penalty. I am very happy.”Of Doku, he said: “He made an impact. This is the reason they are there. Jérémy and the rest – to try to do their best, if they start from the beginning or if they come in from the bench try to make an impact.”The tie might have gone either way, so the lottery of penalties felt apt to decide who went through before Saturday’s rematch back here in the league. City will now play League One Bradford in the quarter-finals.“I watched all [Brighton’s] Premier League games and since the first day they always go front foot, man to man, so they’re going to be exactly the same on Saturday,” Maresca said.His opposite number spoke of vengeance. “We lost in a shootout. We had enough chances to win the game – they had the luck today. We have to reset. We have a great chance on Saturday to take revenge,” said Fabian Hürzeler.Quick GuideCarabao Cup quarter-final drawShowFleetwood v Everton or NewcastleManchester City v Bradford CityCrystal Palace v SunderlandLiverpool v BournemouthTies will take place during the week commencing 14 DecemberWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Brighton will stay up in the area. “Not sleeping in your own bed is not an advantage,” said the manager. “But we’ll go there with full energy and ready to go on Saturday.”When Yalcouyé opened the scoring there was the proverbial hint of offside about the forward as his shot pinged off Rulli and in.With no video assistant referee in theCarabao Cupthe goal stood, though it was soon cancelled out by Kovacic: Phil Foden fed him and, from the edge of the penalty area, he threaded the ball beyond Steele low into the left corner.View image in fullscreenGeorginio Rutter fires Brighton into a second-half lead.Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty ImagesFor the second half Maresca introduced Rayan Aït-Nouri and Ryan McAidoo for Ayyoub Bouaddi and Floyd Samba. Instantly, though, City conceded: Brighton slipped through the lines with ease, and Jaouen Hadjam’s cross was slid in by Rutter.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe forward’s grin went wide in celebration and the Seagulls were heading through, while City were going out. Aït-Nouri, skipping down the left, tried to do something about this, but his ball over was aimless.At least there was pace in this foray, which those in blue sometimes lacked. But, also, Maresca’s team had become sloppy – a long-range Rayan Cherki pass that ended in Steele’s gloves was emblematic.Olivier Boscagli’s corner that dipped viciously close to Rulli’s goalline was far more dangerous, so just after the hour Maresca introduced a first big gun – Doku, for Allan – this coming after Rutter ran in and went close to a second, underlining Brighton’s ascendancy.When Doku played Aït-Nouri in through the left, it was a rare City attack and showed the value of having the Belgian now able to affect the game.At this point, though, the decision to allow his star quintet the night off was backfiring for Maresca. City lacked control and were toothless. Doku, again, cut through Brighton but there were no runners to prosper from his delivery infield.Hürzeler’s men tried to squeeze time and snaffle the ball whenever City attempted to move them about, but then came a first passage in which City camped in Brighton territory. Suddenly, those in green were having to answer questions. Foden’s burst that drew a free-kick from Rutter near the 18-yard line presaged one they could not answer. Cherki blasted at goal, Reis stuck out a boot, Steele was wrongfooted, and it was 2-2. Doku had lit up City, his presence terrorising Brighton’s defence and turning the tie.“They are in a brilliant moment, scoring goals, many goals every game and winning, so we knew it was a tough game in terms of defending in the right way,” Maresca said. “We could have probably done something better defensively, but we started just three months ago [together]. The game was chaotic but we controlled it quite good.”Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupManchester CityBrighton & Hove Albionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Nketiah takes Crystal Palace past Fulham and earns Sage breathing space | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Eddie Nketiah put Crystal Palace into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, beating Fulham 1-0, relieving the pressure on the Palace manager Pierre Sage
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Eddie Nketiah put Crystal Palace into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, beating Fulham 1-0, relieving the pressure on the Palace manager Pierre Sage
Content: Eddie Nketiah’s deft flick from just inside the penalty area earned Crystal Palace victory at Fulham.Photograph: Nigel French/PAView image in fullscreenEddie Nketiah’s deft flick from just inside the penalty area earned Crystal Palace victory at Fulham.Photograph: Nigel French/PACarabao CupNketiah takes Crystal Palace past Fulham and earns Sage breathing spaceEd Aaronsat Craven CottageWed 28 Oct 2026 17.53 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 21.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“Can we play you every week?” chanted theCrystal Palacefans as they celebrated a fifth victory over Fulham on their own patch in the space of 18 months. Eddie Nketiah’s first-half goal against the run of play eased some of the growing pressure on Pierre Sage as Palace booked a third consecutive appearance in the quarter-finals of this competition.The good news for Sage is that Arsenal – who beat them on both of those occasions –have already been eliminated. However, he knows that Saturday’s game at Tottenham will have much more bearing on whether he is still around by the time Palace’s Carabao Cup campaign resumes against Sunderland in mid-December.Rulli’s heroics earn Manchester City shootout success against BrightonRead moreFor Álvaro Arbeloa, this was a disappointing setback after a couple of weeks of progress.Fulhamhave not beaten Palace at Craven Cottage since January 2005 – a run of 10 matches – and will not get a better chance after Sage made 10 changes, including the inspired return of their captain, Dean Henderson, in goal. His save in stoppage time from Gonzalo García proved crucial and there were boos for Fulham at the final whistle. Arbeloa will be relieved that at least he does not have to face Palace again this season.Sage left the pitch blowing kisses in the direction of his wife in the stands, but praised the travelling supporters for helping his team get over the line. “I like the fans, but I love my wife,” he said. “All the fans are really behind us – they are happy when the team is like this. The connection is better when we fight on the pitch.”Fortunes have contrasted significantly for these two sides sincePalace’s 3-2 win here at the start of September. Successive 1-0 victories against Hull and Coventry in the Premier League took some of the heat off Arbeloa but he was disappointed that a rotated side, which still contained several key players, could not take their chances – an issue becoming a recurring theme under the Spaniard. “It’s the same story – we need to learn to be more clinical,” said Arbeloa. “It’s a really frustrating night for everyone.”Quick GuideCarabao Cup quarter-final drawShowFleetwood v Everton or NewcastleManchester City v Bradford CityCrystal Palace v SunderlandLiverpool v BournemouthTies will take place during the week commencing 14 DecemberWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Sage had no choice but to rotate his side heavily after their exertions last week, which included travelling to Istanbul for a draw with Beskitas in the Europa Leaguebefore losing to Newcastle at homethree days later. No doubt with an eye on Saturday’s trip to north London that could define the Frenchman’s future, Chris Richards was the only player to retain his place. There has been talk of a protest before Palace’s next home game against Liverpool over rising ticket prices and what some supporters have described as the club’s strategy “which prioritises tourists instead of regular match-going fans” by playing loud music before kick-off and half-time. The fans who packed the away section were in full voice throughout, even as their second-string struggled against opponents who were clearly brimming with confidence.View image in fullscreenPierre Sage, who has been under scrutiny following some poor results, applauds the Crystal Palace fans after the match.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersFulham went close twice in the space of 60 seconds when Kenny Tete headed wide from a corner before Henderson – after month on the sidelines – saved well with his feet from Antonee Robinson at the far post. Joachim Andersen should have done better with the next chance from another corner soon after, but the Denmark defender could not hit the target against his former club.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWith Cheick Doucouré making his first senior appearance in midfield since January 2025 after a litany of injury problems, Palace looked rusty all over the pitch and did not manage a single touch in Fulham’s box during the first half-hour, amassing just 22% of possession. But they still managed to take the lead when Óscar Mingueza found space down the right flank and delivered an inch-perfect cross for Nketiah to volley in expertly. After all their dominance, Fulham’s supporters could hardly believe their eyes.Palace should have been punished when Honest Ahanor gave the ball away on the edge of his area but Rodrigo Muniz’s shot was weak. Arbeloa turned to his bench and there were huge cheers for Josh King’s arrival. But Jefferson Lerma and Henderson somehow managed to clear Iwobi’s header off the line as Fulham finally created a chance their pressure merited.The Palace substitutes Daichi Kamada and Dwight McNeil could have sealed the victory with late chances as Fulham pushed forward in desperation for an equaliser. Their supporters could not hide their frustration at full-time as Palace’s sang about another possible trip to Wembley. What a difference a few days make.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupFulhamCrystal Palacematch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Howe, Nagelsmann, Pochettino: can anyone end Manchester United’s doom loop? | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: Even an elite coach would surely struggle at Old Trafford amid the executive chaos and with an unfit, uneven squad
Author: Daniel Harris
Headline: Even an elite coach would surely struggle at Old Trafford amid the executive chaos and with an unfit, uneven squad
Content: Fans of Manchester United let their feelings be known  in a protest outside Old Trafford before the Premier League match against Manchester City in September 2026.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFans of Manchester United let their feelings be known  in a protest outside Old Trafford before the Premier League match against Manchester City in September 2026.Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedHowe, Nagelsmann, Pochettino: can anyone end Manchester United’s doom loop?Daniel HarrisEven an elite coach would surely struggle at Old Trafford amid the executive chaos and with an unfit, uneven squadWed 28 Oct 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 16.49 EDTShareIn January 2014 the 13th series of Celebrity Big Brother aired in the UK, the show so popular that its run time was extended by five days before a public vote anointed Jim Davidson the winner. Then, two years later when Brexit happened, people wondered where their tolerant country had gone, lamenting the ephemeral spirit of London 2012 as though the 2011 riots were some kind of fever dream, not a desperate response to decades of structural and institutional racism exacerbated by the cruelty of unnecessary austerity.The truth is that if security is quickly upended, it was built on quicksand to begin with. Which brings us to Manchester United, easing effortlessly from an uplifting third-place finish tosome of the worst footballin their history.An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeurRead moreIt is entirely possible that Alex Ferguson made a deal with the devil to the effect that United would be great until he retired and hilariously dreadful thereafter. But assuming not, hisl’état, c’est moimentality was busy setting up the post-him fall even at the height of the success – itself a consequence of what had gone before.A day after the Munich air disaster, Louis Edwards – later a seller of condemned meat to schools – joined the board, eventually assuming control thanks to a dodgy rights issue. He bequeathed the club to Martin – his substellar son – who floated it for personal gain, turning an institution that sought to win, entertain and unify into a business legally compelled to return value to shareholders.This left United vulnerable to acquisition by anyone and, whenFerguson fell out with two directors– a horse, a horse, his kingdom for a horse’s ejaculate – they sold to the Glazers, who loaded the purchase price and accordant interest obligation on to the club, with government and football authorities waving through a move since outlawed. Ferguson, meanwhile, must have feared exactly what the takeover would entail and known that without his support the banks might not have lent the money, while thechief executive David Gill admitted opposition to it but stayed in his roleanyway, and so the pillaging began.View image in fullscreenManchester United fans let their feelings know about Malcolm Glazer’s proposed takeover of the club in May 2005.Photograph: John Peters/Manchester United/Getty ImagesThe English game then exploded, with investment in United left available only to those of wealth so extreme it necessarily casts aspersions over their character – such asarch polluterand anti‑immigration zealot, Jim Ratcliffe. Proclaiming inaccurate and divisive rhetoric contrary to the inclusive, cosmopolitan spirit of Manchester and United, jobs were culled and fights picked with fans, Old Trafford’s most desirable seats socially cleansed so the club could sell them to day-trippers for astronomical prices, with longstanding supporters banned aftertrumped-up charges of touting– a deeply principled stance the club fails to apply to itself.Not untypically for a billionaire, Ratcliffe seemingly believes that correct opinions reflect exchequer not expertise, giving himself final say on footballing decisions. And rather than the “best in class” executives he promised, his United operate according to what political analysts call the “Boris principle”, no‑marks in thrall to their own self‑image given jobs for which they lack the ability and character, the consequent chaos being effective sabotage.So the patterns continue: Champions League qualification is missed, insufficient funds are released; a new unsuitable manager spends heavily on players below requisite standard; Champions League qualification is achieved via unsustainably reactive style; the manager is denied necessary funds amounting to less than the bounty of Champions League qualification; the manager imposes a proactive style without the necessary materials; the manager is belatedly fired for a fee far exceeding that saved by cutting jobs; a new unsuitable manager, with entirely different requirements to his predecessor, is appointed; executive accountability is absent.View image in fullscreenEddie Howe is the preferred choice of director of football Jason Wilcox if there is a change of manager at Old Trafford.Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/ReutersIt is thus no surprise thatMichael Carrick remains unfired, despite exuding the vibe of a man who’s mentally fired himself. Perhaps it’s a stay of execution, but more likely there’s bizarre hope of a turnaround, partly to save paying him off, partly because the relevant executives can’t achieve consensus on a replacement, and partly because surely even Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox accept that, following another catastrophe, after dismissing Carrick they are honour-bound to dismiss themselves.Except they and United don’t work like that.So, just as they failed Carrick bynot recruiting properly; failing to add experience to his coaching team; failing to replace outgoing fitness and set-piece coaches and failing to interrogate details of his new game-model, they are now failing him by having him continue in a job that is too much for him, destroying a season that remains salvageable. Meantime, the Glazers’ dividends continue unabated.As such, the question isn’t so much who should be United’s next manager as can anyone manage United? Increasingly, it looks like the answer is – to quote Don Logan in Sexy Beast – “No”.There are immediate on‑pitch issues: the team are unfit and their collective mentality weak; after years being lied to, the captain has finally broken; and the players hate the suits, the package toxic. Those are the minor problems.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRoughly, football management comprises five aspects: coaching, tactics, talent ID, pastoral care and presence. And, though no manager excels in every department, at this version of United surely they must. Moreover, given this is no job for a novice, track record is also important – and it might be here that Unai Emery’s candidature falls down, his brilliance in transforming mid‑ranking clubs undermined by failures at two high-profile basket cases.View image in fullscreenMauricio Pochettino has recently signed a contract extension which puts him in charge of the USA men’s team until 2030.Photograph: Kirby Lee/Imagn Images/ReutersWhich brings us to pastoral care and presence. In the postwar era, onlyErik ten Hag has won a trophy at Unitedwithout tangible charisma, the size of the club now demanding it more than ever. This is not a quality associated with Eddie Howe, while Antonio Conte does not scream pastoral care and, brilliant though his career has been, he failed miserably at Spurs, the only environment he has inhabited that is remotely similar to United.Should United miss Champions League qualification, financial strictures will make an elite coach and tactician essential. But in any event, football has changed such that the alchemic art of combining players and personalities no longer guarantees success.Which leaves us with talent ID, player quality and intelligence being the best coaching and tactics there are. Of the 78 players purchased post-Ferguson, only Bruno Fernandes and perhaps Zlatan Ibrahimovic could be classed as cast-iron successes, so the next man – assuming United don’t target Emma Hayes, who embodies more of the right stuff than almost anyone else – must have a keen nose. Even Jürgen Klopp, the other manager who fulfils these criteria – and of all the damage Ed Woodward wreaked on United, turning him off was most costly – benefited from a department which delivered the greatest run of transfers ever.View image in fullscreenGermany’s coach at the 2026 World Cup, Julian Nagelsmann, speaks to his squad. He is believed to be admired by Manchester United’s executives.Photograph: Pilar Olivares/ReutersWhich leaves Mauricio Pochettino, who built something at Tottenham despite the environment, and Julian Nagelsmann. But had Pochettino not signed a new contract with the USA men’s team, the sense is that, as when Mourinho arrived at Old Trafford after years of speculation, he’s past his magical best, while Nagelsmann may be the free-thinking genius of his own imagination, just as he may be an emperor’s new clothes bluffer.All of which is to say that failure has many fathers and, once ingrained, is not easily eradicated. Yet just as society has too much going for it to ever move quite beyond the pale, so too doesManchester United. Even the longest journey starts with one step; but does anyone have the nous to ensure it’s taken in the correct direction?Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarrickJim RatcliffecommentShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: McInnes booed in Rangers draw at Hearts, Celtic held at home | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Derek McInnes was booed on his return to Tynecastle, where Rangers drew 2-2, which was also the score between Celtic and Dundee United
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Derek McInnes was booed on his return to Tynecastle, where Rangers drew 2-2, which was also the score between Celtic and Dundee United
Content: Olwethu Makhanya jumps between two Hearts defenders for Rangers’ second.Photograph: Zak Mauger/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOlwethu Makhanya jumps between two Hearts defenders for Rangers’ second.Photograph: Zak Mauger/Getty ImagesScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: McInnes booed in Rangers draw at Hearts, Celtic held at homeDerek McInnes returns to Tynecastle for 2-2 drawMartin O’Neill ‘disappointed’ by Dundee United resultAgencies andGuardian sportWed 28 Oct 2026 19.25 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 20.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOlwethu Makhanya scored a late equaliser asRangersearned a 2-2 draw withHeartson the much-hyped Tynecastle return for Derek McInnes.The Rangers manager was booed loudly by the home support as he emerged from the tunnel for his first match back since leaving for Ibrox in June, just weeks after the Edinburgh side were pipped to theScottish Premiershiptitle.Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progressRead moreHowever, his team silenced a pumped-up home crowd when Kevin Kelsy scored a 16th-minute opener after a lapse from Laurent Mendy.Hearts turned the game round with goals from Cláudio Braga and Calvin Miller early in the second half. But Makhanya’s 89th-minute header ensured the match ended all square, keeping second-placed Rangers four points behindCelticand four above Hearts.Celticshowed their mettle as they fought back to grab a 2-2 draw withDundee Unitedat Parkhead.The Colombian striker Camilo Durán put Martin O’Neill’s team ahead in the 18th minute with his 11th goal of the season. But the Australian forward Zac Sapsford levelled in the 28th minute with a header before the defender Neil Farrugia put the visitors in front three minutes later with his first goal for the club.Celtic piled forward in the second half and the defender Liam Scales equalised with a 64th-minute header. O’Neill said: “We cannot control anything that’s happening elsewhere. The disappointment and the frustration comes from not winning a home game.“That’s really it. But considering the trials and tribulations over the last number of weeks, yeah, I’m not totally dissatisfied. We conceded some poor goals, but we fought back and I just thought we were going to win it. But in the end we could have lost it too, on the break. I thought Dundee United were very dangerous and they played very well in the game.”View image in fullscreenCeltic’s Liam Scales rises highest to make it 2-2 against Dundee United.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAStephen Robinson, theAberdeenmanager, admitted his side were not good enough in the 1-0 defeat byFalkirk, but refused to shout and scream at his players in the aftermath.Ben Brauhaus, on as a substitute, scored the only goal of the game, side-footing into the bottom-left corner from the centre of the box after 73 minutes.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRobinson, though, felt his side should have scored from at least one of their chances before then, saying: “Not good enough. We got what we deserved. We had four chances we should score. We had four great chances from inside the penalty spot, and we should score.“All four are very, very easy chances. We don’t do that, they take their one chance, and that’s why you don’t win football matches.”Ash Hay piled more pressure on theKilmarnockmanager, Neil McCann, after scoring a late double to earnDundeea 3-1 win at Dens Park. His strikes, in the 83rd minute and the fifth minute of added time, gave his side the win after Joe Hugill’s 75th-minute penalty.Hibernianmoved off the bottom of the table as they drew 1-1 atSt Mirrento secure Marink Reedijk’s first point as manager. Marko Ivezic put Hibs ahead but Jason Kerr’s own goal denied them a third league win this season.Motherwellended a six-match losing run but they were denied a victory as Josh Campbell’s 93rd-minute equaliser forSt Johnstoneearned them a 2-2 draw. Taylor Steven had given the home side the lead before Ibrahim Said and Tawanda Maswanhise turned the scoreline around. However, Campbell’s late header sealed a point.Explore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipHeartsRangersCelticDundee UnitedAberdeenFalkirknewsShareReuse this content

title: Carabao Cup roundup: Bournemouth thrash Villa, Sunderland salvo stings Bees  | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Bournemouth and Sunderland swept into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with home wins against Aston Villa and Brentford respectively
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bournemouth and Sunderland swept into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with home wins against Aston Villa and Brentford respectively
Content: Amine Adli (21) of Bournemouth scores the opening goal beating Marco Bizot (40) of Aston Villa.Photograph: Graham Hunt/ProSports/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenAmine Adli (21) of Bournemouth scores the opening goal beating Marco Bizot (40) of Aston Villa.Photograph: Graham Hunt/ProSports/ShutterstockCarabao CupCarabao Cup roundup: Bournemouth thrash Villa, Sunderland salvo stings BeesCherries win 3-0 to set up Anfield visit in last eightWearsiders resist Brentford fightback in 3-2 successPress AssociationWed 28 Oct 2026 19.15 EDTLast modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 20.22 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBournemouthcontinued their impressive run of results by thumpingAston Villa3-0 to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals for the first time in eight seasons, while Sunderland scored three times in 10 minutes at the Stadium of Light to leave Brentford too much to do as the home side won 3-2.The winger Amine Adli fired home in the seventh minute at the Vitality Stadium to set Marco Rose’s in-form side on course for a fifth consecutive win in all competitions. Lewis Cook, the Cherries captain, added a fortuitous second early in the second period before the striker Álvaro Rodríguez sealed another 3-0 success after similar wins against Milan and Manchester United.Villa – five-time League Cup winners – were second best for most of a fruitless trip to the south coast as they endured a first defeat in eight games. Taylor Harwood-Bellis and the substitutes Alejandro Garnacho and Alysson had the visitors’ best chances in Dorset butBournemouthregistered a fifth clean sheet in a row to ease into the last eight.Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties yet again to secure Carabao Cup progressRead moreBoth sides made wholesale changes for the fourth-round tie. Adli – one of eight players brought in by Rose, the Bournemouth head coach, finished a fine team move to open the scoring.After James Tavernier unlocked the visitors’ defence with a delightful ball over the top, the full-back Julio Soler delivered a lofted cross from the left, allowing the Morocco international Adli to fire into the top-right corner from six yards out.Villa’s unfamiliar lineup struggled to create in the opening stages and only a smart stop from the goalkeeper Marco Bizot prevented Ben Gannon-Doak extending Bournemouth’s lead.George Hemmings flashed wide as Unai Emery’s team eventually threatened before the 17-year-old striker Brian Madjo was denied by a smothering save from the home goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio.Bournemouth doubled their lead six minutes into the second half.
